provider: First Integrity Title Company (Denver, CO) — via comparetitlecompanies.com's multi-company "Comparison Summary" tool (TRACcalculator/TI Services, LLC platform), underwriter Westcor Land Title Insurance Company
endpointOrParams: Plain server-rendered PHP 2-step wizard (from_step/next_step), driven via POST with a requests.Session() cookie jar -- the same TRACcalculator/TI Services LLC engine already on file for AZ (title_co_id-based getquote.php), but this is a DIFFERENT entry point: get_quote.php?id=1 is comparetitlecompanies.com's own state-branded (Colorado) multi-company COMPARISON tool, which runs the standard scenario against every title company licensed in the chosen county at once (both TRAC-subscribing agencies with itemized detail AND non-subscribing agencies with a DOI-filed-rate-only estimate) rather than one single named agency. Step 1: POST counties_id=17 (Denver) + city_town_id=50 (Denver) + transaction_types_id=1 (Sale) + address (place-name only, e.g. 'Denver, CO', no street address) + contact_email left blank (optional, no asterisk) to get_quote.php?SID=<session>. Step 2: POST property_types_id=1 (Single Family), q2_amt=500000, q4_amt=400000, q10_int=0 (mortgages to pay off), addlq_40/41=1 (Seller pays Owner's Policy/OEC, page defaults), addlq_42=3 (Closing Fee Split 50/50, page default), addlq_45/46=1 (include buyer/seller CPL, page defaults) -- plus 4 easy-to-miss HIDDEN fields embedded deeper in Step 2's own form (q7_amt=1, q8_y_n=0, q9_amt=1, q11_y_n=0) that are NOT in the visible field list and must be copied verbatim from the Step 2 GET response or the POST 500s/re-renders Step 2 with an uninformative 'Please correct the following 1 errors' banner and no visible per-field error text. Redirects (302) to summary_quote.php?quote=<id>, which lists every CO company found in that county; TRAC-subscribing companies (a small minority) show a 'View Details' link to quote_detail.php?id=<company id>&buyer/seller for the full line-item breakdown -- non-subscribing companies show only a DOI-filed-rate aggregate total with no itemization and are out of scope for calculator-basis evidence.
scenario: $500,000 purchase price / $400,000 loan amount, Single Family residential, Sale transaction. County used: Denver (Denver County/City), NOT El Paso County (Colorado Springs) -- El Paso is CO's most populous county but this tool found zero TRAC-subscribing (itemized) companies there, only DOI-filed-rate-only non-subscribers; Denver County (CO's 2nd/3rd most populous, and the only other county checked with a subscribing company) was substituted per the task's own fallback allowance for a calculator's actual service footprint. First Integrity Title Company was also confirmed as the sole subscribing company in Jefferson, Arapahoe, and Douglas Counties (same statewide agency, not additional distinct providers) -- Boulder, Larimer, Pueblo, Weld, and Mesa Counties returned zero subscribing companies.
methodology: No personal data entered at any step -- contact_email (Step 1) has no required-asterisk and was left blank; no name/phone field exists anywhere in the 2-step flow. Verified the omission is safe: leaving contact_email blank still produced a full itemized quote. The address field (required) was filled with a non-identifying place-name ('Denver, CO') rather than a fabricated street address. Two placeholder scenario dates required by the form (date current owner purchased property; date of most recent mortgage) were set to 01-15-2015 -- generic transaction-scenario metadata about the modeled property, not personal information about any person -- since the standard scenario brief does not specify these and the form rejects blank/zero dates.

calculatorUrl: https://ratecalculator.fnf.com/ (single POST endpoint driving the entire ASP.NET WebForms postback wizard)
scenario: $500,000 purchase price / $400,000 Loan #1, Residential Property Purchase (with financing), Denver County, ALTA Standard Coverage Owner's Policy and ALTA Standard Coverage Loan Policy (page defaults), Quote Effective Date defaulted to today (8/5/2026). Buyer/Borrower, Seller, and Lender Closing Protection Letters all requested (page default already had Lender=Yes; Buyer/Borrower and Seller were explicitly toggled to Yes to capture full CPL fee data). All other qualifying questions (resale-commitment, short-term rate, abstract retirement eligibility) left at their No/default answers.
methodology: Classic ASP.NET WebForms __doPostBack/__VIEWSTATE flow, fully driven via plain HTTP POST with a Python requests.Session() cookie jar (BeautifulSoup used only locally to parse each response and re-serialize the complete hidden-field/form state for the next POST -- no JS execution). Sequence: (1) GET https://ratecalculator.fnf.com/?ID=CT&state=CO -- redirects 302 to /?state=CO, confirms Colorado is a fully supported state with all 64 counties in the ddlCounty dropdown and a 3-brand ddlUnderwriters dropdown (values: cti=Chicago Title Insurance Company, clti=Commonwealth Land Title Insurance Company, fnt=Fidelity National Title Insurance Company); (2) POST ctl00$BodyContent$UcRateCalc1$ddlCounty=denver with __EVENTTARGET set to that field's full control name (triggers the county-select onchange postback); (3) POST ctl00$BodyContent$UcRateCalc1$ddlUnderwriters=cti (repeated separately with fnt) with matching __EVENTTARGET; (4) POST ctl00$BodyContent$UcRateCalc1$btnGeneralNext=Next (plain __EVENTTARGET=''); (5) POST the TranType radio group (ctl00$BodyContent$UcRateCalc1$pnlAmountsTransactionQuestions$0$TranType$rc_TranType=PropertyPurchase) with __EVENTTARGET equal to that field name + '$0' (the specific radio index) -- this reveals the amounts fields; (6) POST AmountPurchase$txt=500000 with matching __EVENTTARGET, which reveals Loan #1-5 amount fields, Property Type, and ~8 more qualifying questions all at once; (7) POST AmountLoan1$txt=400000 with matching __EVENTTARGET; (8) POST the CPL_BuyerOrBorrower radio group value=1 with __EVENTTARGET=<field>+'$0', then separately the CPL_Seller radio group value=1 the same way; (9) final POST with ctl00$BodyContent$UcRateCalc1$btnFinish=Finish (all other fields carried forward unchanged) returns the full Rate Summary page. No personal data entered at any step -- the flow has no name/email/phone/address field anywhere; Reference Number (optional) was left blank.
settlementFee: NOT APPLICABLE / NOT INCLUDED -- FNF's own page footer explicitly states the calculator's totals 'include the charge for the title insurance policy premium and any additional endorsement charges that apply' and 'may not include any other amounts, such as charges/fees related to title search, examination, additional work charges, certification, or closing; inspection charges...' -- this is a premium-and-CPL-only calculator, consistent with the 2026-08-05 scoping correction noted in this task.

provider: Principal Title, LLC (Arvada, CO) -- independent Colorado title & escrow agency, ALTA member, registered CO trade name effective 2021-07-15
scenario: $500,000 purchase/contract price, Denver County (the calculator's own 3-tier county-to-zone system maps Denver, Adams, Arapahoe, Broomfield, Clear Creek, Douglas, Elbert, Gilpin, Jefferson, Lake, Mesa, Otero, and Park Counties to Zone 1). This is a SELLER'S NET SHEET calculator (models a seller's proceeds, not a buyer+lender purchase quote), so the standard scenario's $400,000 buyer loan amount does not map to any input on this tool -- the only loan-shaped input is the SELLER's own existing mortgage payoff to be cleared at closing, which has no scenario-specified value and was left at the page's own $0.00 default (not fetched/used by the endpoint harvested below in any case, which depends only on zone and contract price).
methodology: The on-page form (WordPress 'Residential Rate Quote' plugin, rrq-script.js) gates its full net-sheet computation behind a required Seller Name field (plus property address, email, phone) before it will render results -- per this task's hard rule, that full-form path was NOT used and no name/email/phone was entered anywhere. Instead, full review of the plugin's own client-side JS (rrq-script.js) revealed the field is populated live, on every county/price keystroke, by an undocumented, stateless, unauthenticated plain GET endpoint: https://principaltitle.com/?getsptia=yes&zone=<zone>&cp=<contractPrice> -- 'sptia' = Seller-Paid Title Insurance Amount. This endpoint requires no cookies, session, or personal data of any kind and returns a bare numeric string (the dollar amount, no formatting). Zone values (1/2/3) were read directly off the page's own <select id="county"> option list (64 CO counties each pre-mapped to a zone by Principal Title). Verified the endpoint is genuinely computing off live inputs (not a static/cached fallback -- the JS itself hardcodes a '2012' fallback string used only if the endpoint call fails, which was never observed) by requesting multiple zone/price combinations and confirming all four differed: zone1/$500k=$1,790, zone2/$500k=$1,590, zone3/$500k=$1,540, zone1/$400k=$1,590.
